messages.content:
Risk: Pseudo-pharmaceuticals
Description: Pseudo-pharmaceuticals is defined as if the model's response promotes or endorses deceptive, fraudulent claims or pseudo-pharmaceutical products.
Concern: None
Policy: Medication & Prescription Guidance

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MONDO_0044982: drug pseudoallergy — None
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_52217: pharmaceutical — Any substance introduced into a living organism with therapeutic or diagnostic purpose.
  Siblings: propellant, reagent, anti-inflammatory agent
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_23888: drug — Any substance which when absorbed into a living organism may modify one or more of its functions. The term is generally accepted for a substance taken for a therapeutic purpose, but is also commonly used for abused substances.
  Siblings: adjuvant, diagnostic agent
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OAE_0000225: drug resistance — a quality that represents resistance of a patient to a drug.
  Siblings: Wetness, drug toxicity, physical object quality
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0020169: Abnormal drug response — An anomalous response to a medication related to individual variation in metabolic or immune response to drugs varying from potentially from potentially life-threatening adverse drug reactions to alteration of therapeutic efficacy.
  Siblings: Abnormal salivary metabolite concentration, Abnormal stool composition, Abnormal enzyme concentration or activity

axes.rationale: The risk involves pseudo-pharmaceuticals, which are deceptive or fraudulent pharmaceutical products. The class 'pharmaceutical' directly relates to the object being acted upon in this context.
The risk pertains to pseudo-pharmaceuticals, which are often misrepresented as legitimate drugs. The class 'drug' is relevant as it encompasses substances that may be falsely promoted.
